title: Finite EHKICK bends sloped particles on the wrong radius and leaves yp unchanged
summary: A finite-length EHKICK with a nonzero kick mistracks particles with nonzero vertical slope y′: it uses total momentum to set the projected bend radius and changes horizontal slope x′ while keeping y′ fixed. A uniform vertical field conserves total and vertical momentum, requiring a helix whose radius depends on momentum perpendicular to the field, as independent Lorentz-force integrations confirm. For a 0.7 m magnet with a 0.09 rad kick, a particle 20% above reference momentum entering with x′ = 0.08 and y′ = 0.06 leaves with y′ = 0.06000 instead of 0.06054, losing 0.8842% of its vertical momentum. At 1 mrad kick and slopes, y′ is 1.500 nrad too small; particles without vertical slope are unaffected.

title: KQUAD given by pole-tip field and bore tracks its fringes with zero strength until a matrix or Twiss request
summary: KQUAD can be specified by pole-tip field B and bore radius BORE instead of normalized gradient K₁. With nonlinear fringes enabled and K₁ left at its default zero, the body uses the field-derived strength but both fringes use zero strength until a matrix or Twiss output request overwrites K₁. The same beam then leaves the same magnet differently depending on whether optics output was requested; after the request it matches the equivalent explicit K₁. For a 0.4 m magnet with K₁ = 5 m⁻² and electron momentum 2000 mₑc, exit slopes change by up to 1.749 µrad and positions by up to 95.29 nm. Pole-tip quadrupoles with enabled fringes are affected.

title: KQUAD fringes ignore the fractional strength error FSE that scales the body
summary: KQUAD scales its body's normalized gradient by 1 + FSE, where FSE is the fractional strength error, but both nonlinear fringe kicks keep the unscaled gradient K₁. A uniform field error leaves the fringe profile normalized to the central gradient unchanged, so K₁ = 5 m⁻² with FSE = 0.2 must track like K₁ = 6 m⁻² with FSE = 0, and FSE = −1 must be a plain drift. For a 0.4 m magnet and electron momentum 2000 mₑc, the exit slopes differ by up to 419.4 nrad, and at FSE = −1 the exit position is displaced by up to 54.35 nm. Field-error scans with fringes distort the fringe-to-body ratio.

title: MODRF damped phase modulation keeps an undamped local frequency
summary: With damped phase modulation, MODRF uses a local angular frequency that is not the derivative of its bunch-centroid phase. The frequency omits both exponential attenuation and the derivative of the damping envelope, so the energy variation within the bunch disagrees with the specified phase waveform. The manual specifies the same local-frequency formula.

title: UKICKMAP loss compaction gives survivors extra radiation updates
summary: With classical radiation enabled in UKICKMAP, removing an out-of-map particle can apply one extra radiation update to the survivor moved into its place. Independent radiation-integral recurrences and no-loss and loss-last controls establish the extra update.

title: Yawed kick maps sample half a slice behind the particle
summary: In GKICKMAP and UKICKMAP, yaw alignment evaluates the map-axis displacement at the slice entrance after the particle has drifted to the slice midpoint. title: LSRMDLTR radiation loss scales with the cube of the reference momentum
summary: With classical radiation enabled in the LSRMDLTR laser modulator, an electron's calculated momentum loss changes when only the reference momentum changes. For particle momentum p and reference momentum p₀ in units of mₑc, the implemented local loss rate is (p₀/γ)³ times the classical rate, where γ = √(1 + p²) is the Lorentz factor. At p = 1200 in a 0.8 m, eight-period, 0.8 T undulator, classical loss on the same integration grid is 2.383×10⁻⁴ mₑc; tracking gives 2.979×10⁻⁵ at p₀ = 600, 2.312×10⁻⁴ at 1188 and 1.906×10⁻³ at 2400. Off-reference radiation calculations are biased, including about 3% for a 1% reference change.

title: Initial moments omit shared-dispersion covariance terms
summary: With moments_output matched=0, equilibrium=0, explicit Twiss, dispersion and longitudinal inputs produce a covariance matrix Σ for (x, x′, y, y′, s, δ) missing eight terms, where s is longitudinal position and δ is relative momentum offset. For independent betatron motion, dispersion η requires cross-plane covariances ηᵢηⱼΣ₆₆ and transverse–longitudinal covariances ηᵢΣ₆₅. For longitudinal emittance ε_z = 1 μm, β_z = 4 m, α_z = 0.2, η_x = 0.1 m and η_y = −0.03 m, Σ₁₃ must be −7.800×10⁻¹⁰ m² and Σ₁₅ −2.000×10⁻⁸ m², but both are zero. Propagated covariance matrices inherit the error. Nonzero momentum spread with dispersion in both planes, or dispersion with longitudinal position–momentum correlation, triggers the error.

title: Zero-length MULT quadrupole cubic matrix contains infinities
summary: The third-order transfer map of a zero-length quadrupole, MULT with L=0, ORDER=1 and integrated strength KNL = 0.6 m⁻¹, contains infinite cubic coefficients. Concatenation contaminates 336 map coefficients with NaN, including R₂₁, which should be −0.6000 m⁻¹; finite second-order and short-length controls isolate the singular thin-lens construction. For a thin-lens FODO cell using cubic lens maps, horizontal tune νₓ has d²νₓ/dδ² and d³νₓ/dδ³ equal to NaN instead of 0.2030 and −0.06786, where δ is the relative momentum offset. Users requesting third-order optics for zero-length MULT quadrupoles are affected.

title: Analytic QUAD cubic chromatic coefficients are wrong
summary: Elegant's aligned, hard-edge QUAD writes incorrect third-order matrix coefficients for transverse transport proportional to δ², where δ is the relative momentum offset. For length L = 0.5 m and strength K₁ = 0.6 m⁻², exact transport has R₁₁(δ) = cos(u/√(1+δ)), with u = √(K₁) L, giving U₁₆₆₁ = −0.07222; Elegant writes −0.07245, with relative errors across both planes of 0.1853% to 0.6598%. In a one-period FODO cell using cubic lens maps, d²νₓ/dδ² and d³νₓ/dδ³ are 0.1300 and −0.07925 instead of 0.1268 and −0.08637, where νₓ is the horizontal tune. Users of third-order quadrupole optics and higher-order chromaticities are affected.

title: Higher chromaticities mix cell and repeated-period phases
summary: With `higher_order_chromaticity=1` and `n_periods=2`, Elegant's `twiss_output` converts single-cell trace derivatives using the repeated lattice's phase, producing wrong second and third chromaticities. On a continuous phase branch, a stable cell's tune ν and every momentum derivative must scale with the period count. For 0.5 m `KQUAD`s with K1 = 0.6 and −0.54 m⁻² and 1 m drifts, one period gives d²νₓ/dδ² = 0.1268 and d³νₓ/dδ³ = −0.08637, where δ is the relative momentum offset. Two periods require 0.2537 and −0.1727, but the output gives 0.1865 and −0.3286; the tune and first chromaticity scale correctly. Users computing higher chromaticities of repeated cells are affected.

title: Quartic path term enters cubic momentum compaction
summary: Elegant's `twiss_output` reports the third-order momentum compaction `alphac3`, the δ³ coefficient of the relative path length with δ the relative momentum offset, but adds a product of two second-order dispersions that belongs to δ⁴. For a prescribed stable 10 m cell with second-order term T166 = 0.2 m (closed orbit x = 0.1 m·δ²) and path term T511 = 0.3 m⁻¹ (path length ∝ x²), the path is 10 m + 0.003 m·δ⁴, so `alphac3` must be 0, but Elegant writes 3.000×10⁻⁴. Tracking 12 particles on the closed orbit reproduces the quartic path, and removing either term gives zero. Users optimizing or matching `alphac3` are affected; physical rings were not assessed.

title: MULT pole-tip optics use electron rigidity for other species
summary: For `MULT` quadrupoles specified by pole-tip fields, analytic optics use electron rigidity even when `change_particle` selects positrons or protons. For a 0.4 m magnet with bore radius 0.02 m, integrated pole-tip field 2.000×10⁻⁵ T·m and dimensionless momentum p/(mc) = 10, the physical horizontal slope response R₂₁ is −0.05844 m⁻¹ for electrons, +0.05890 m⁻¹ for positrons and +3.195×10⁻⁵ m⁻¹ for protons; the analytic matrix gives −0.05844 m⁻¹ for all three. The positron and proton focusing signs are reversed, and the proton |R₂₁| is 1829 times too large. Direct tracking and explicit integrated strengths agree with the physical quadrupole matrix. Users computing these non-electron optics from pole-tip fields are affected.

summary: With `twiss_output matched=0`, Elegant uses exit dispersion where the chain rule requires entrance dispersion to compute chromatic beta functions and phase advances. title: Quick second chromaticity translates a supplied closed orbit twice
summary: With `quick_higher_order_chromaticity=1`, Elegant shifts a one-turn map by the closed orbit after it has already been expanded about that orbit, corrupting the second chromaticity d²ν/dδ², where ν is tune and δ is relative momentum offset. For a prescribed cubic map with a closed orbit 10 mm off axis and a momentum-independent Jacobian there, the exact horizontal derivative is 0; quick mode gives −0.08750 and full mode −3.198×10⁻¹⁰. In this map, halving the displacement reduces the error fourfold, while an on-axis orbit or removal of the cubic term leaves only fitting noise. Users of quick chromatic optics with off-axis closed orbits and cubic nonlinearity are affected.

title: Slice normalized emittances omit the mean momentum offset
summary: Elegant's `slice_analysis` normalizes each longitudinal slice's geometric emittance with the reference momentum instead of the slice's mean momentum, while the whole-beam normalization includes the mean momentum offset. Reference momenta of 450 and 1350 mₑc produce 1.080×10⁻⁴ and 3.240×10⁻⁴ m; even references 1% below or above the slice momentum give −1% or +1% errors, and the dispersion-corrected values behave identically. Users reading normalized slice emittances when a slice's mean momentum differs from the reference are affected.

title: Manual gives the third-order momentum compaction term as δ² instead of δ³
summary: The Elegant manual gives the path length as s = s₀ + αc L δ + αc2 L δ² + αc3 L δ², with δ the relative momentum offset, for the Twiss outputs `alphac`, `alphac2` and `alphac3`. title: Pelegant falsely warns that fast-orbit-feedback BPM readings are not reduced across ranks
summary: When a user runs the fast orbit feedback command under MPI (Pelegant), Elegant warns that beam-position-monitor (BPM) readings are not reduced across ranks, which would leave each rank's monitor reading only its own particles. With 24 particles split between two tracking ranks whose local means differ, the monitor instead reads the whole beam's mean, as products of lens and drift matrices predict, for one and three turns per readout and feedback gain 0 or 0.2500: 3.474×10⁻⁴ m horizontally and 3.150×10⁻³ m vertically after one turn. The warning is therefore false for these readings and can lead users to discard valid parallel runs, although the manual says Pelegant results are identical to serial for a deterministic beam.

title: Round nonlinear space charge omits the integrating length and optics weighting
summary: With `insert_sceffects` and `nonlinear=1`, SCMULT omits the integrating length and optical weights from the kick of a round Gaussian beam. The branch is selected when the rms sizes σₓ and σᵧ satisfy |σₓ − σᵧ|/σₓ < 10⁻⁶; an unsliced Gaussian control with σᵧ/σₓ = 1.00001 agrees with an independent integrated-field calculation. In a symmetric ring with 1 nC of electrons at 10 mₑc and σₓ = σᵧ = 1 mm, the round kick is 4.000 times the correct value after a 0.25 m drift and 1.333 times it after a 0.75 m drift. Round-beam nonlinear space-charge studies in rings are affected.

summary: With `insert_sceffects` set to `nonlinear=1`, SCMULT ignores the `horizontal` and `vertical` switches that enable space charge in each plane. title: Uniform nonlinear space charge is too weak by √12
summary: With `insert_sceffects`, `nonlinear=1` and `uniform_distribution=1`, SCMULT's unsliced coasting-beam prefactor is 1/√12 = 0.2887 of its correct value for both round and elliptical beams. An independent Gaussian transverse-field integral with uniform number density N/(√12 σₛ), where N is the particle population and σₛ the rms longitudinal length, establishes the missing normalization. In an 8 m ring with 1 nC of electrons at 10 mₑc and 1 mm rms transverse sizes, a sampled round-beam particle after a 1 m drift receives −3.558×10⁻⁷ rad instead of −1.233×10⁻⁶ rad, a 71.13% suppression. Linear controls obey their own force law, and the 1 m round-beam case removes the separate integration-weight error.

title: Single-precision reciprocals in the complex error function reduce the Gaussian force accuracy
summary: Nonlinear SCMULT kicks for elliptical Gaussian beams lose accuracy when the SDDS complex error function evaluates its power-series reciprocals in single precision despite a 14-digit accuracy contract. For 1 nC of electrons at 10 mₑc with rms sizes 2 mm horizontally and 1 mm vertically, a sampled particle's horizontal kick is −3.149×10⁻⁵ rad, differing from the independent Poisson-integral value by −7.904×10⁻¹³ rad (2.510×10⁻⁸ relative). A scalar model reproduces the native kicks with single-precision reciprocals and agrees with the integral to about 10⁻¹⁵ relative with double-precision reciprocals. Accumulated effects over many turns have not been measured.

title: WAKE cache substitutes the first requested column pair
summary: When two WAKE elements in one Elegant run select different wake columns (WCOLUMN) or time columns (TCOLUMN) from the same table file, the second element silently reuses the first element's columns, because the table is cached by file name alone. For a table with kernels A and B = 3A, the earliest particles of a 12-electron, 2 nC bunch should lose the sum of both kernels, 8000 eV; the shared file gives 4000 eV (A applied twice) or 12000 eV (B applied twice), depending on element order, which is an error of -50% or +50%. A byte-identical copy of the table under another file name gives the correct result. Anyone who selects several kernels from one wake file is affected.

title: Broadband ZTRANSVERSE doubles its DC impedance
summary: Broadband ZTRANSVERSE sets its zero-frequency impedance to 2Rₛ/Q instead of the documented Rₛ/Q, where Rₛ is the shunt impedance and Q the resonator quality factor. title: Broadband ZTRANSVERSE uses the wrong Nyquist frequency and sign
summary: Broadband ZTRANSVERSE evaluates its highest resolved (Nyquist) impedance at the next frequency index and reverses the real part's sign. With 50 ps bins, a resonator of shunt impedance 1×10⁶ Ω/m, quality factor 1 and resonant frequency 1 GHz should have −9999 Ω/m at the 10 GHz endpoint; the element uses +9994 Ω/m. For a 2 nC electron beam at 50 mₑc, six particles at +1 mm horizontal offset and six at −1 mm in adjacent bins, the 8192-bin calculation adds errors of ±3.821×10⁻⁹ rad relative to an independent Fourier sum and impedance-table control. The error alternates between bins, shrinks with a longer window and affects beams with an alternating transverse source moment.

title: BEAMBEAM kicks change arrival time because s is not rescaled
summary: A BEAMBEAM kick changes momentum but leaves the stored longitudinal coordinate s = βct unchanged, where t is arrival time, c is the speed of light and β is speed divided by c. The output time therefore changes by the ratio of incoming to outgoing speed, although the zero-length element must preserve time and rescale s. For an electron of momentum 1 mₑc at horizontal position x = 0.2300 mm, a 1.300 nC uniform opposing bunch of radius 1.300 mm changes an input time of 1 µs by −1.936×10⁻¹¹ s, a relative error of −1.936×10⁻⁵. Zero input time masks the error, and all three source distributions are affected.

title: Dipole resonators create momentum in the disabled plane
summary: When TRFMODE or FTRFMODE tracks a dipole mode in one plane only, its longitudinal kick creates momentum in the other plane in proportion to the incoming slope there. title: Later SCMULT bunches use the exit beta function for the entrance weight
summary: When Elegant tracks a bunch train with SCMULT space-charge kicks (`insert_sceffects` in bunch mode), every bunch after the first integrates the space-charge strength over each element with the element's exit beta function β in place of its entrance value, so identical bunches receive different kicks. Where β falls from 0.9141 m to 0.8018 m along a 0.3 m drift, the second and third of three identical bunches receive 6.542% less kick than the first, with linear and nonlinear forces alike. title: SCMULT size-filter history is shared between bunches
summary: Nonlinear SCMULT bunch-train tracking with size-averaging factor 0 < f < 1 uses one shared size history per element: after the first turn, each bunch filters against history last updated by another bunch instead of its own previous turn. In this independent-bunch model, changing another bunch must not change the kick; an isolated bunch checked against an independent Gaussian-field integral supplies the control. At momentum 17 mₑc, charge 0.2000 pC per bunch and f = 0.4000, making a second bunch 2.500 times wider changes the first bunch's second-turn horizontal slope kick on its first particle from 2.510×10⁻⁹ to 4.532×10⁻⁹; making it 2.500 times longer changes it to 2.733×10⁻⁹. Multi-bunch ring simulations using size averaging are affected.

title: Empty SCMULT slice centroids break translation symmetry
summary: Linear SCMULT tracking with time slicing and slice interpolation leaves empty slices' transverse centroids at zero instead of using the whole-bunch centroids specified by the manual. Mixing those values with occupied slices breaks translation symmetry: a common transverse displacement changes the self-kicks, whose mean must remain zero for the symmetric test bunch. For 20 electrons carrying 0.2000 nC in 100.0 ps slices with one empty neighbor, a displacement of (1.700, −2.200) mm produces a mean horizontal slope of 5.597×10⁻⁶ instead of zero. Sliced ring simulations that interpolate with an empty neighbor are affected; extrapolation can also reverse the erroneous mean.

title: MPI SCMULT mixes bunch statistics when a rank holds no particles of a bunch
summary: When two bunches are distributed one per tracking rank, linear unsliced SCMULT space-charge tracking under MPI (Pelegant) merges their statistics. title: Sliced linear SCMULT normalizes every slice by the whole-bunch beam size
summary: With constant matched optics, linear SCMULT space-charge forces, slicing on (`slice_duration` > 0), interpolation off and slice populations meeting `slice_threshold`, Elegant normalizes each slice's field gradient by the whole bunch's rms widths. The manual instead treats each slice independently; for transverse rms widths σₓ and σᵧ, its horizontal gradient is proportional to 1/[σₓ(σₓ + σᵧ)], as equal-width and isolated-slice controls confirm. For two equal-charge slices whose widths differ by a factor of 2, the narrow slice's gradient is 9.742×10⁻⁷ m⁻¹ instead of 2.436×10⁻⁶ m⁻¹, 2.500 times too weak, while the wide slice's is 1.600 times too strong. Ring simulations with unequal slice sizes are affected.

title: Constant RFMODE frequency waveforms repeatedly scale stored voltage
summary: In single-bunch RFMODE tracking, a constant frequency multiplier a supplied through FREQ_WAVEFORM, with FREQ divided by a to preserve the resonant frequency, scales the stored beam-induced voltage by √a on every traversal. A stationary passive cavity should follow the same damped response as the direct-frequency setting, which agrees with an independent parallel-RLC circuit calculation. For quality factor Q = 11.00, shunt impedance RA = 200.0 kΩ, frequency 0.8300 GHz and a 0.3000 nC electron bunch represented by 18 macroparticles, the fifth-traversal tail energy loss is 9366 eV for a = 1.440 or 1.247×10⁴ eV for a = 0.2500, instead of 1.015×10⁴ eV. title: TRWAKE quadrupole probe coordinates omit element misalignment
summary: TRWAKE quadrupole wakes (probe exponents 1, drive exponents 0) use each particle's global transverse coordinate even when the structure has misalignments DX and DY. The kick must use displacement from the structure, so translating beam and structure together must preserve the kicks, and a beam on the structure's axis must receive none. For a 0.6000 nC electron bunch represented by 18 macroparticles, a common shift of (3.100, −1.700) mm raises the trailing particle's horizontal slope kick from 1.498×10⁻⁵ to 6.660×10⁻⁵, and an on-axis beam receives 5.161×10⁻⁵ instead of zero. Dipole wakes, with probe factor 1, pass the translation controls.

title: Single-bunch TRWAKE fixed bins retain a zero time reference
summary: With a fixed TRWAKE bin count (N_BINS > 0) and a single bunch, Elegant anchors the grid to time zero rather than the bunch and omits particles outside it as both wake sources and recipients. summary: With multiple bunches and a fixed TRWAKE bin count (N_BINS > 0) under MPI (Pelegant), each tracking rank centers its histogram on its own bunch mean, so unequal rank means make summed bins represent different physical times. title: MPI TRWAKE combines different bunches when ranks skip locally empty bunches
summary: With automatic bins and bunch mode, TRWAKE tracking under MPI (Pelegant) combines different bunches when each of two tracking ranks holds one whole bunch. title: SCMULT manual prints the averaging filter with the current turn in its history term
summary: The manual's nonlinear SCMULT averaging equation uses σ̂ᵢ = fσᵢ + (1−f)σ̂ᵢ, where f is `averaging_factor` and σᵢ and σ̂ᵢ are the actual and filtered rms beam sizes on turn i. title: MATTER collision slices omit incoming transverse drift
summary: When MATTER uses single scattering in a finite-length target, each slice containing a collision omits the transverse drift from the slope entering that slice. Correct transport must include that slope times the slice length, in addition to the displacement from the scattering kick. In a one-slice, 0.01 m helium target, shifting the incoming horizontal and vertical slopes by 0.002 and −0.003 leaves all scattered electrons' exit positions unchanged, instead of shifting them by 20.00 µm and −30.00 µm; unscattered electrons drift correctly. Users tracking sloped beams through finite-length material are affected, and earlier kicks can also expose the error in later slices.

title: Standalone electron recoil omits energy loss
summary: In MATTER, enabling ELECTRON_RECOIL while ENERGY_DECAY and NUCLEAR_BREMSSTRAHLUNG are disabled omits the documented recoil energy loss. The energy-processing gates ignore standalone recoil, although collisions with target electrons must transfer positive energy. For 20000 electrons of momentum 1000 mₑc crossing 0.01 m of dilute helium, a Poisson approximation to the option's event rate predicts 6894 ± 67.21 electrons losing energy, but recoil-only output is bit-identical to all-off output. Enabling bremsstrahlung activates thousands of recoil losses, isolating the activation failure. Users enabling recoil alone are affected.

title: Active recoil transfers use inconsistent energy normalization
summary: For relativistic electrons in MATTER with ELECTRON_RECOIL and NUCLEAR_BREMSSTRAHLUNG enabled, recoil-transfer rates are suppressed by about the momentum P, measured in mₑc, at transfers above binding energies and small compared with incident kinetic energy. The event rate contains 1/P, but sampled transfers are subtracted directly from the Lorentz factor γ. For 20000 electrons at P = 1000 crossing 0.01 m of dilute helium, the free-electron Møller integral predicts 42.22 electrons losing at least 1.022 keV; serial and three-rank parallel runs give none despite active recoil sampling. The Poisson probability of zero such transfers under that reference is 4.408×10⁻¹⁹. Users modelling collisional energy-loss tails are affected.

title: Smooth IBS ignores the plane switches DO_X, DO_Y and DO_Z
summary: With the smooth method (SMOOTH=1), an IBSCATTER element applies the intrabeam-scattering growth to all three planes whatever the plane switches DO_X, DO_Y and DO_Z say. With all three switches at 0 the beam should leave the element unchanged, as it does for FACTOR=0, and with one switch at 1 only that plane should change. Users who disable one plane of smooth IBS, or all of it, are affected.

title: Smooth IBS shifts the beam centroid when there is dispersion and a momentum offset
summary: With the smooth method (SMOOTH=1), IBSCATTER measures the beam centroid c and scales the transverse coordinates about c + ημ, where η is the dispersion and μ the beam's mean fractional momentum offset δ. The centroid already contains the dispersive displacement ημ, so the origin is displaced twice and the centroid moves by (1−a)ημ, where a is the amplitude growth factor, instead of staying fixed. In a closed ring with η = 14.29 m and μ = 1×10⁻⁴, an amplitude growth of 0.8501% moves the mean horizontal position by −12.14 µm instead of 0; with μ = 0 it stays put. Users of smooth IBS with dispersion and an off-momentum beam are affected.

title: CBSCAT computes a negative Klein–Nishina total cross section just above its Thomson cutoff
summary: When Elegant's CBSCAT element, which models laser Compton scattering, uses its default Klein–Nishina cross section, the total cross section it evaluates just above ε = 10⁻⁶ can be negative, where ε is the laser photon energy in the electron rest frame divided by mₑc². Cancellation between large terms destroys the result, and then no electron scatters. For 25 mₑc electrons, a head-on laser and a Thomson probability of 0.025, the code's total is −28.95 times the Thomson value at ε = 1.200×10⁻⁶ instead of 1.000, and none of 24000 electrons scatters instead of about 600; at ε = 5.000×10⁻⁶ the ratio is 0.6069 and 345 scatter. Users with ε of a few 10⁻⁶ are affected.

title: Approximate CBSCAT recoil depends on the reference momentum
summary: With the approximate recoil of Elegant's CBSCAT element (CROSS_SECTION="thomson", EXACT_RECOIL=0), the momentum an electron loses in a laser Compton scatter depends on the reference momentum P₀ the user chose, although the physics does not. The code computes the fractional change ΔP/P of the electron's momentum P and adds it to δ = P/P₀ − 1, which requires ΔP/P₀. For 12 mₑc electrons and a 30 µm laser, the same 454 scattered electrons lose a mean 2.303×10⁻⁵ mₑc at P₀ = 12 mₑc, 1.152×10⁻⁵ mₑc at P₀ = 6 mₑc and 4.607×10⁻⁵ mₑc at P₀ = 24 mₑc. title: Thin forced-MCS MATTER omits the flight distance from the transverse angles
summary: With FORCE_MCS=1 in a MATTER element thinner than 0.001 radiation lengths and ENERGY_DECAY=0, Elegant advances the longitudinal coordinate by the axial length L alone. At speed βc, the flight time must be at least √(L² + Δx² + Δy²)/(βc), where Δx and Δy are transverse displacements between the endpoints. In dilute helium with L = 0.4 m, electrons at momentum 2.000 mₑc with slopes (0.001, 0.003) violate this bound by 7.459×10⁻¹⁵ s; at 2.400 mₑc with slopes (−0.02, 0.015), the deficit is 4.516×10⁻¹³ s. Arrival-time calculations through thin targets or residual gas with forced scattering are affected.
